title: Strategic Thread Consolidator and Commitment Windows
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Create a single canonical registry (the Strategic Thread Consolidator) that maps company-level OKRs to cross-functional initiatives with clearly defined Commitment Windows (timeboxed delivery bands) and decision rights. The registry will be the source of truth for roadmap gating, capacity allocation, and escalation during the quarter.

Background: Multiple teams currently propose initiatives against the same top-level objectives with overlapping scopes and unclear handoffs. This causes duplicate work, late re-scopes, and downstream SLA surprises. The Consolidator will: 1) normalize initiative boundaries, 2) expose capacity conflicts early, 3) provide program-level milestones tied to measurable OKR signals, and 4) publish Commitment Windows that define when an initiative can claim runway/capacity.

Scope: Company-level (OKR Tier 1–2) initiatives and any cross-functional projects that materially impact platform throughput, Dedicated/Private offering readiness, or billing/SLAs. Not in scope: feature-level sprint tickets, purely localized experiments, or infra chores under 3 points unless they influence a Tier 1 metric.

Success metric: Reduced cross-team re-scoping events by 50% (tracked in the registry), fewer unplanned dependencies in the last two weeks of a cycle, and improved on-time milestone attainment for company OKRs.
acceptance_criteria: A single searchable registry page exists (Confluence) listing all company-level initiatives mapped to OKRs with owners and Commitment Windows
Each listed initiative includes: primary owner, supporting teams, key milestones, success metrics (linked to dashboard), and top 3 risks
Program-level capacity conflicts are surfaced weekly and have documented mitigation plans or arbitration owner
Commitment Windows are defined (start/end per initiative) and honored in >= 80% of cases or have recorded exception approvals
A 1-pager governance runbook is published that describes triage flow, arbitration path, and handoff checklist
